items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 17, overrideLimiter=true — parsed fresh from the 26.1.2 ParticleTypes <clinit>) with a dedicated ElderGuardianParticle$Provider (ParticleResources.registerProviders, offsets 296-300) and spawns it on game event GUARDIAN_ELDER_EFFECT (ClientPacketListener.handleGameEvent, offset 520; addParticle at the player position, offset 530, plus the curse sound at 574 — all re-read from the 26.1.2 client jar; all three classes byte-identical to 26.1.1's). The port's ParticleType enum (127 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets (lan_particles.rs:488), /particle rejects it (particle.notFound, world_cmds.rs:760), and override_limiter() misses it (28 vanilla vs 27 real-26.1.2 Rust entries). Unlike 1.21.7, the 26.1.2 providers driver does NOT send elder_guardian cases (omitted from the 120-kind set), so the defect blocks no driver here — it silently skips the type. The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime, mob_blocks.rs:70/79), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Particle::read decodes wire id 42 (flash, verified against the 26.1.2 registry) as Color(i32) — a flash particle always carries a colour — but hub_particle has no Flash arm in its Color match (EntityEffect | TintedLeaves only, lan_particles.rs:437), so the packet is built with data None and Particle::write (writes data by presence, not id) emits the id with no colour bytes; guests reading id 42 consume the next 4 stream bytes as the colour and desync. Reachable only via /particle flash on a LAN host (cmd_particle builds ParticleOptions::simple(ty) via the catch-all, world_cmds.rs:871; Flash is otherwise created client-side only, in firework explosions, particles.rs:3777); the local player draws directly and is unaffected. entity_data.rs and world_cmds.rs are byte-identical to the 26.1.1 tree's; lan_particles.rs differs only in two comment lines.
items.title: /particle minecraft:flash sends a malformed packet to LAN guests (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 registers SPRUCE_LEAVES as TintedParticleLeavesBlock with leafParticleChance 0.01 (Blocks.class is byte-identical to 26.1.1's, so the 26.1.1 parse carries exactly: BlockItemIds.SPRUCE_LEAVES -> lambda$static$27 -> TintedParticleLeavesBlock(0.01F); LeavesBlock.animateTick rolls nextFloat() < chance). The port maps spruce_leaves to Animate::Leaves(None, None, false) — no falling particle (animate_tick.rs:151, file byte-identical to 26.1.1's). All 10 other leaf blocks match vanilla (cherry 0.1, pale oak 0.02, rest tinted 0.01; azalea fixed colour -9399763 matches exactly). The marker driver would fail its spruce zoo cases (oracle emits, probe emits none — the probe runs the port's real animate_tick, marker_particles_probe.rs:168); the driver's own comment ('the spruce that never falls', test_marker_particles_parity.py:114) encodes the same wrong belief and needs correcting with the fix.
items.title: Spruce leaves never drop falling-leaf particles (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 has no SpeleothemBlock class at all (0 entries in either jar; PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly) and no speleothems tag; the prepared data agrees (pointed_dripstone class chain is [PointedDripstoneBlock, Block] in block-behaviours.json). Vanilla LevelEventHandler routes 1504 to PointedDripstoneBlock.spawnDripParticle with no class gate (offset 3508, verified fresh). The client routes 1504 to dripstone_drip_particle (game.rs:4376-4377), whose first act is the is_stalactite gate (level_particles.rs:243-244): has_class("SpeleothemBlock") is false for every block in 26.1.2, so the drip particle never spawns. The ambient animateTick drip path is unaffected (name-based table, animate_tick.rs:397-410). Whether the port's server actually transfers fluid to cauldrons in 26.1.2 (G6's status) is Batch 5's scope; the client gate is dead regardless.
items.title: Level-event 1504 stalactite drip particle never fires: is_stalactite gates on SpeleothemBlock, absent in 26.1.2 (reproduces from 26.1.1)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2's ParticleGroup.add is a plain queue add (javap -c on the 26.1.2 client jar: particles.add(p), no size check, no probability roll); the class declares MAX_PARTICLES (16384) but never enforces it — the cap is a 26.2 addition. ParticleGroup.class is byte-identical to 26.1.1's. The 26.1.2 port's tick_tracking (particles.rs:3880, the drain that moves every created particle from pending into the live list — create() pushes to pending, :2087) enforces the cap (:3925-3935): at 16,384 live particles every new particle is dropped, and above 12,288 new particles are dropped with probability 1 - ((16384-size)/4096)^2, drawing the level random for each rejection (constant at :1349-1350). The 26.1 tree deliberately has NO cap here (its comment documents the cap as 26.2-only). The cap only bites in particle-heavy scenes (above 12,288 live particles); below that threshold the port matches vanilla exactly.
items.title: Particle engine enforces the 16,384 group cap vanilla 26.1.2 never enforces (26.2-form; the 26.1 tree deliberately removed it)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2's TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect is a record with ONE field (diameter: float) — no directional_particles field — and its apply calls LivingEntity.randomTeleport(x, y, z, true), which broadcasts entity event 46 (128 portal particles at the entity; LivingEntity.handleEntityEvent case 46, offsets 392/410). Vanilla LevelEventHandler has NO 2017 case (79-case lookupswitch). The 26.1.2 tree carries the 26.3 form inherited from 26.1.1: TeleportConsume has a directional_particles: bool field (teleport_consume.rs:6); items.rs:124 reads it from data with unwrap_or(true), and the prepared 26.1.2 data never carries the field (chorus_fruit consumable is {"on_consume_effects": [{"type": "minecraft:teleport_randomly"}]}; 0 occurrences of directional_particles in items.json), so it defaults to true; teleport_consume.rs:109-121 fires the event on every successful teleport and the client impl (consume.rs:422-431) calls level_event_at(2017, ...), routed (game.rs:4338-4341) to consume_teleport_particles -> block_teleportation ([127,127,127], particles.rs:1848), 128 portal particles along the old->new line. The port ALSO fires the vanilla-correct event 46 (consume.rs:188-194, remote.rs:4782-4784), so a chorus-fruit teleport shows BOTH the correct burst AND a second, wrong directional trail. The 26.1 tree has no directional_particles anywhere.
items.method: javap + source + data + tree diff vs 26.1.1
items.title: Chorus fruit shows an extra 2017 directional teleport trail vanilla never sends, on top of the correct event-46 burst (26.3-form; the 26.1 tree has no such event)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2's EnderMan.teleport calls randomTeleport(x, y, z, true) (offset 110) -> entity event 46 -> 128 portal particles at the entity; the only addParticle call in EnderMan is the ambient aiStep emission, not the teleport. LevelEventHandler has NO 2018 case. The 26.1 tree's mobs/enderman.rs documents this explicitly ('26.3 also fires the level event 2018 portal trail; 26.1 has no such event here'). The 26.1.2 tree's teleport_to (mobs/enderman.rs:161-190) pushes BOTH the vanilla-correct entity event 46 AND MobEvent::LevelEvent { id: 2018, ... } (when not silent), routed (game.rs:4343-4346) to enderman_teleport_particles -> enderman_teleportation (particles.rs:1873), 128 portal particles along the old->new line. Every enderman teleport shows the correct burst plus a second, wrong trail. (The destination-selection half of the enderman rework — the tag form — is Batch 3's scope, B3-G14; only the particle-visible trail is minted here.)
items.title: Enderman teleport shows an extra 2018 directional portal trail vanilla never sends, on top of the correct event-46 burst (26.3-form; the 26.1 tree omits it)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2's Shulker.teleportSomewhere does: unRide, setAttachFace, playSound(SHULKER_TELEPORT), setPos, gameEvent(TELEPORT), set peek data, setTarget — no randomTeleport, no addParticle, no broadcastEntityEvent, no level event anywhere in the class (0 such references in the full javap -c dump, 26.1.2 server-game jar). A shulker teleport in vanilla shows zero particles. LevelEventHandler has NO 2016 case. The port's mobs/shulker.rs:366-371 (byte-identical to 26.1.1's and 26.1's) pushes MobEvent::LevelEvent { id: 2016, ... } on every teleport. In the 26.1 tree this event is dropped (game.rs has no 2016 arm), so the 26.1 port accidentally matches vanilla. The 26.1.2 tree keeps the handler inherited from 26.1.1 (game.rs:4333-4336 -> shulker_teleport_particles -> block_teleportation [8,8,8], particles.rs:1848), so every shulker teleport now shows 128 portal particles along the old->new line that vanilla never shows. Unlike G06/G07 there is no correct event-46 burst underneath — the trail is the ONLY particle output and it is entirely wrong.
items.title: Shulker teleport shows a 2016 directional trail; vanilla shows NO particles at all (the 26.1 tree drops the event and accidentally matches vanilla)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2's MultiPlayerGameMode never calls addBreakingBlockEffect anywhere in the class (0 occurrences in the full javap -c dump), and LevelEventHandler has NO 2019/2020 cases. startDestroyBlock plays nothing and spawns nothing; continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound, on destroy ticks 0, 4, 8, ... (destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0, volume (volume+1)/8, pitch * 0.5, offsets 197-262) — no particle at any point while digging. The 26.1.2 tree keeps the 26.1.1 form: breaking_block_effects (level_particles.rs:351-373: hit sound when play_sound, plus crack_particle — one crumb on the mined face), called from startDestroyBlock (remote.rs:8180, breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true)). The port's server never sends 2019/2020, so the network dispatch (game.rs:4298-4306) is dead and the continue path plays NOTHING. Net effect vs vanilla: an extra crack particle + a hit sound at the first hit (vanilla: silence), then silence for the rest of the dig (vanilla: a hit sound every 4th tick). The 26.1 tree is correct here (start plays nothing; continue plays sound-only on ticks 1, 5, 9, ...). The particle half (extra crumb) is minted here; the sound-schedule half is flagged for Batch 10.
items.title: Digging shows a crack particle (and a mistimed hit sound) vanilla never shows; the every-fourth-tick hit sound is missing (26.2-form breaking effects; the 26.1 tree is sound-only)

items.evidence: Batch 7-routed flag (B7 report §8.6 / slice out_of_scope_failures in the 26.1.1 run), verified fresh here. Vanilla 26.1.2's SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe (javap -c, 26.1.2 server-game jar) is y < maxY && !state.liquid() && !state.is(BlockTags.FIRE) — no teleport tag. The #entities_can_teleport_to tag does not exist in 26.1.2: 0 entries in either jar's datapack, absent from the prepared block-tags.json (no teleport-containing block tag at all). The port's spread_safe (world_cmds.rs:2132-2154) returns y < max_y && !liquid && teleportable, where teleportable (:2141-2146) requires membership in #entities_can_teleport_to — always false in 26.1.2. So spread_safe is ALWAYS false; in the spread loop (:2018-2026) every collision-free iteration re-randomizes every point, collisions stays true, and the loop runs until iteration >= 10_000, when the command fails with commands.spreadplayers.failed.entities (or .teams, :2030-2043). /spreadplayers cannot succeed in the 26.1.2 port on any terrain. Shared with the 26.1 and 26.1.1 trees (world_cmds.rs byte-identical); the 26.1 run's Batch 9 never covered /spreadplayers safety and neither does the 26.1.1 Batch 9 slice — the 26.1.1 run was the first record of the defect. Commands-area; minted here on the coordinator's routing via Batch 7 — the merge may re-route it to Batch 9's ledger.
items.method: javap + data + source (Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh)
items.title: /spreadplayers always fails: spread_safe requires the #entities_can_teleport_to tag, which 26.1.2 does not have (shared with the 26.1.1 tree; missed by the 26.1 run)

items.evidence: The providers driver's SIMPLE list carries red/orange/yellow_poplar_leaves (26.3-only) plus sulfur_bubbles and sulfur_cube_goo (26.2-only) — the 5 the 26.1 report named — AND the driver's cases() generator also yields noxious_gas, noxious_gas_cloud, geyser, geyser_plume, geyser_base, geyser_poof (test_particle_providers_parity.py:94-105, 6 more kinds, 72+ cases), which the 26.1 report wrongly said were never sent ('The geyser kinds are NOT in the driver's kind set ... so they need no trim' — incorrect; they are yielded by the same cases() generator make_cases consumes). method: Static analysis only (no driver runs, no cargo tests, no commits — per the batch brief; prepared 26.1.2 data exists in .local/horizon-client/26.1.2/). Jar-identity first: 40 particle-relevant classes md5-compared between the vanilla 26.1.1 and 26.1.2 jars, all byte-identical — where a 26.1.1 jar finding rests on one of those classes it carries verbatim; every claim was additionally javap-verified fresh against the 26.1.2 jars (LevelEventHandler lookupswitch, ParticleGroup.add, MultiPlayerGameMode, LivingEntity.randomTeleport/handleEntityEvent, Shulker.teleportSomewhere, EnderMan.teleport, DragonEggBlock.teleport, SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe, LocalPlayer ctor, ParticleTypes <clinit> parsed from the javap -c dump, ParticleResources provider registration, ClientPacketListener game event, TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect record shape, oracle APIs). Registry census from 26.1.2's own prepared + datagen registries.json (117 types, identical, ids contiguous 0-116). Source comparison against versions/26.1.2/crates/ plus a full tree diff against versions/26.1.1/ for every particle file (all byte-identical except lan_particles.rs, comment-only); data checks against the 26.1.2 datagen reports (registries.json, blocks.json) and the prepared data (registries.json, block-behaviours.json, block-tags.json, items.json). Oracle triage from the measured Batch 0 table (docs/sweep/26.1.2/batch-0-oracles.json), with the two failing particle oracles re-verified against the 26.1.2 jar. The Batch 7-routed /spreadplayers flag was verified fresh (javap + data + source) and minted as B8-G10.

Sound flags for Batch 10 (particle halves verified here, sound halves not minted): 3003 wax-on sound missing from the level-event path (vanilla plays HONEYCOMB_WAX_ON from the event; the 26.1.2 tree kept the WAX_ON particles but dropped the sound — the item-use/dispenser/remote/golem wax sounds are all still present, so the missing case is a client receiving the 3003 event for someone else's waxing); 2002/2007 splash-potion break sound missing (vanilla plays SPLASH_POTION_BREAK from the event; the 26.1.2 tree maps it to events 1053/1054, which vanilla 26.1.2 never sends); digging hit-sound schedule (sound half of B8-G09: hit sound at first hit instead of every 4th tick, then silence). Not verified (need driver runs): all per-tick provider numerics, emitter/entity-burst RNG draws, marker-loop exactness, the translucent-layer table, sprite-set resolution, level events other than 1504, 2015-2020 and 3002-3005 (2015's exact RNG-draw equivalence needs a run), apparition visual fidelity, and the dripstone climb-limit off-by-one question (vanilla passes 11 to findBlockVertical; the port climbs 10 steps). 31 particles.rs unit tests unrun. source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 8 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: all 117 particle types, emitters, providers; 8 drivers found in the tree (7 particle-named + effect_sync, particle-adjacent; the plan claims 9, the 9th is unaccounted for). DRAFT: not committed — checks + triage only per the batch brief. All sixteen 26.1.1 Batch 8 items reproduce in 26.1.2 (10 behaviour defects, 4 needs-harness, 2 oracle defects); no new defects found — the 26.1.1->26.1.2 delta touches nothing in particle scope (every particle file byte-identical except lan_particles.rs, comment-only; all 40 particle-relevant vanilla classes byte-identical between the jars). The 26.1-record corrections are carried (H02: 11 kinds, not 5; the entity-API attribution to LivingEntity; B8-G10 checked fresh).
systemic_note: Same shape as the 26.1.1 batch, with the delta-port twist: the 26.1.2 tree inherits 26.1.1's particle defects exactly — the four reproduced original defects are four different shapes (a missing registry entry carried through every table (B8-G01), a write-path/read-path asymmetry in one codec arm (B8-G02), a wrong per-block belief baked into both the port and the driver's own comment (B8-G03), and a 26.2+-only class name gating a 26.1.2 path (B8-G04)), and the five 26.2/26.3-form reversions (B8-G05–G09) carry over unchanged because every file involved is byte-identical to 26.1.1's. The directional-teleport events are one feature in three defects: 2017/2018 ADD a trail on top of the correct event-46 burst (double particles), while 2016 is pure invention (vanilla shows no particles for a shulker teleport at all). The sixth carried defect (B8-G10, /spreadplayers) is the opposite shape: code shared verbatim with the 26.1 tree that both runs' Batch 9 missed. The positive systemic finding stands: the port's particle tables are otherwise exact — all 117 types covered end-to-end except elder_guardian, all 18 data-carrying wire ids correct, all 28 limiter flags correct except elder_guardian, all 30 entity-burst pairs and all 45 marker-zoo blocks covered, and all 11 leaf blocks' chances verified — the gaps are narrow and enumerated, not a broad drift. The 11 extra types in the Rust enum are dead but unreachable.
